- criteria_path: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/fitness/process-definition.fitness.md
- artifact: /home/vscode/rebaseline/basis/processes/typedef-rendering.md

Judge the artifact against every scenario. Report every finding with the criterion it fails by name, the quoted text, the change, and whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the PM role decides from the review alone. A defect no criterion names is a finding with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean" only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top three changes."

Return exactly this structure:
judge_stamp: <model id> / screen prompt v6
verdict: clean | findings
findings:
- criterion: <scenario name or number, or "uncovered">
  section: <section of the artifact>
  quoted: "<the text>"
  change: <what would repair it>
  decided: confident | wobbly
top_three: <the three most important changes, or "none">

Be literal to the criteria. Do not invent criteria. Do not read any other file. Judge all of it, including the steps YAML and every loop's exit.

# Fitness set: process-definition

These scenarios are evaluated by the `cold-reviewer` role, never
executed; the compiler and linter carry the mechanical half of the
same requirements. The mapping table compiles each Then into the
judge-rubric assertion the reviewer scores. The scenarios project the
[process-definition typedef](../artifacts/process-definition.md)'s
requirements and the
[process-definition guideline](../guidelines/process-definition.md)'s
rules into a judge's rubric.

## Scenarios

Scenario 1: the definition is the single source its renderings claim
  Given the process definition, its flow diagram, and its rendered
  skill
  When the diagram and skill are compared to the steps section
  Then both correspond to the steps exactly — every step, prompt, and
  branch present, nothing added — and both declare themselves
  generated, never hand-edited

Scenario 2: every outcome has a live witness
  Given the outcomes list and the steps section
  When each outcome's named witness is looked up
  Then every outcome names a step, check, or branch that exists, and a
  reader can say from the witness alone whether the outcome held for a
  run

Scenario 3: every loop declares its exits
  Given every cycle in the flow
  When its branch rows are read
  Then each cycle carries a labeled reached-state success exit, a
  round or budget cap, or both — no loop can run unbounded

Scenario 4: steps read only what they list
  Given each step's prompt, checks, and run template
  When every reference in them is resolved
  Then each resolves to a declared input or output of that step, and
  no prompt directs the agent to load undeclared context

Scenario 5: the run returns the artifact
  Given the result declaration and the purpose
  When they are compared
  Then the run returns the artifact it exists to produce, or result is
  absent and the outcomes pin the run's value

Scenario 6: prose sits where prose belongs
  Given every step record and the guiding statement
  When each is read
  Then step prose appears only in prompt fields, and the guiding
  statement (when present) states a cross-step judgment, never a
  sequence

## Compile mapping (each Then/And → one judge-rubric assertion)

| Scenario Then | Judge-rubric assertion |
|---|---|
| 1 — renderings correspond | "Walk the diagram and skill against the steps: name any step, prompt, or branch missing or added, and any rendering not marked generated. Empty list = pass." |
| 2 — outcomes witnessed | "For each outcome, name the witnessing step/check/branch and confirm it exists. Any outcome with a missing or unverifiable witness = fail, cite it." |
| 3 — loop exits declared | "List every cycle and its labeled exits. Any cycle without a success exit or cap = fail, cite it." |
| 4 — declared reads only | "For each step, quote any reference in prompt/checks/run that is not a declared input or output, and any prompt directing undeclared context loads. Empty list = pass." |
| 5 — artifact result | "Name the result value and what the purpose says the run produces. Mismatch, or a status-shaped result = fail; absent result justified by value-pinning outcomes = pass." |
| 6 — prose placement | "Quote any prose in a step outside prompt, and quote the guiding statement if it sequences steps. Empty list = pass." |

## Sources

Gherkin syntax (readable G/W/T frame — syntax only, no runner);
G-Eval–style rubric decomposition for the mapping table; the tests
project the process-definition typedef's checklist and Commitment and
the guideline's rules, per the definition-chain shape the
principle-set chain established.

1 --- 2 type: process-definition 3 id: typedef-rendering-process 4 owner: product-authority 5 status: draft 6 version: 1 7 created: 2026-09-05 8 updated: 2026-09-05 9 produces: [] 10 carried-by: typedef-rendering-skill 11 condition-language: cel 12 annotations: 13 claude-code: 14 activation: model-judged 15 promotion: experiment-local 16 use-when: "an approved typedef carrying its writing rules and fitness scenarios changes or lands, a guideline or fitness set at its load point stands in doubt — missing, not current with its typedef, written by hand, or left by a typedef that no longer qualifies — or the shop must confirm that every such typedef has both of its texts current" 17 --- 18 19 # Process: Typedef rendering 20 21 **Purpose:** Keep the two texts of every artifact type current with 22 the type's one standard. An *artifact type* is a kind of document the 23 shop produces; its *typedef* is the single source the type is 24 generated from, a definition under `basis/artifacts/`. A typedef that 25 stands approved and carries a "Writing rules" section and a "Fitness 26 scenarios" section is the type's standard, and this process calls such 27 a typedef *qualifying*. Its two texts are *renderings* — generated 28 outputs, never edited by hand, never the source: the *guideline*, the 29 maker's text, the type's writing rules read by whoever makes an 30 artifact of the type; and the *fitness set*, the checker's text, the 31 judged Given/When/Then scenarios a check screens an artifact against. 32 Each stands at a *load point*, the directory its readers read it from: 33 `basis/guidelines/` for guidelines and `basis/fitness/` for fitness 34 sets. The process checks what stands at the two load points against a 35 fresh render of each qualifying typedef by the *compiler* — the tool 36 of the *lead shop*, this repository, the shop that owns the product's 37 definitions — that produces both texts from a typedef, and reconciles 38 every difference through the compiler — so that a maker and a checker 39 of the type work from the same words, a change to the typedef reaches 40 both texts, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that they do. 41 42 **Guiding statement:** A rendering is never the source of truth. 43 Whatever stands at a load point that a fresh render of a qualifying 44 typedef would not put there is a finding, and every finding resolves 45 toward the typedef — a re-render by the compiler, a removal, or the 46 owner's decision on the typedef — never an edit to a rendered text, and 47 never an edit to the typedef made to match one. 48 49 **Outcomes:** 50 - O1. Every qualifying typedef has both of its texts at their load 51 points, each byte-equal to a fresh render of that typedef, and the 52 check reports no finding of any kind — witnessed by `route`'s first 53 success exit, on empty `open` with empty `escalations` (feature 54 scenarios 3 and 5: after a run, each text is current with its 55 typedef as it now stands). 56 - O2. The texts land where the checks already read, and nowhere else: 57 a type's guideline at `/.md` and its fitness set 58 at `/.fitness.md`, `` the type key the 59 typedef's `defines` names — the paths the artifact checks and the linter read 60 today — so a check finds the checker's text where it read it before 61 and no check's definition changes for this — witnessed by 62 `reconcile`'s render into those two paths and by `check`'s sweep of 63 those two directories and no other (feature scenario 6). The 64 scenario's other half — a check running from its definition as it 65 stood, its Document History recording no change — is witnessed at 66 delivery, in that check's Document History, not by a step of this 67 process. 68 - O3. A typedef that does not qualify yields no text a maker or a 69 check reads: `enumerate` admits only qualifying typedefs and its list 70 is the set `check` renders against, and a `stale` rendering (O4) is 71 removed at reconciliation — witnessed by `enumerate`'s run, its 72 `approved` read by `check`, and the stale rows of `open` consumed by 73 `reconcile` (the feature's constraint C6). 74 - O4. The check reports every defect as a row of one of five kinds, 75 named here and nowhere else. The row's first word is the kind and 76 its second word its subject; for `missing`, `diverged`, 77 `hand-written`, and `stale` the third word is the path the 78 reconciliation acts on, and `will-not-compile` acts on its subject 79 and carries the reason as the remainder. Three kinds are the 80 compiler's rows, one run per typedef in `approved`: `missing 81 ` — a text absent from its load point; `diverged 82 ` — a text not byte-equal to a fresh render of its typedef, 83 whatever the cause, a hand edit or a typedef amended after its 84 render — where `` is the produced text's id, `-guideline` 85 or `-fitness`, so the row names the text, and `` is 86 the typedef's path, added by `check` as the third word, so the row 87 names the type; `will-not-compile ` — a typedef in 88 `approved` the compiler does not render, its subject the typedef's 89 path as the compiler prints it, and for which the compiler writes 90 no `missing` or `diverged` row, so an unrenderable typedef never 91 also burns the run toward the cap. Two kinds are `check`'s own 92 sweep of the load points: `stale ` — a rendering 93 whose `source` key names a typedef not in `approved`; `hand-written 94 ` — a file at a qualifying typedef's output path 95 that carries no `generated` key; the subject of a sweep row is a 96 path — witnessed by the rows of `findings` that `check` writes 97 (feature scenario 4). 98 - O5. Every finding reaches its consumer and resolves toward the 99 typedef: `missing`, `diverged`, and `hand-written` are re-rendered by 100 the compiler, which produces the type's two texts together, so both 101 are current with the typedef as it now stands after reconciliation; 102 `stale` is removed; `will-not-compile` lands as a review entry in 103 that typedef's Document History. An escalation never ends with the 104 run and never burns it: a row whose subject is already named in 105 `escalations` is not open, so a check clean of open rows with 106 escalations standing routes through `report`, which files each row 107 into the governed record the owner reads — witnessed by `filter`'s 108 run, `reconcile`'s prompt, `route`'s clean-with-escalations branch, 109 and `report`'s prompt (feature scenarios 3 and 5). 110 111 **Roles:** reconciler and reporter — 112 [`../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md`](../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md) 113 (the compilers and the lint are this role's apparatus; it consumes the 114 check's findings, and its resulting action per finding is a re-render, 115 a removal, or an escalation). The owner — the product authority, who 116 owns and approves every typedef — decides every escalated typedef 117 change; that decision lands through governed evolution, not through a 118 step of this process. The check itself is mechanical and runs by the 119 runtime against the qualifying typedefs and the compiler's rendering 120 contract, so the definition of good sits outside the role that 121 reconciles. 122 123 **Carried by:** `.claude/skills/typedef-rendering/SKILL.md` — generated 124 from this definition by 125 [`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never 126 edited by hand, and placed at the skills load point by the 127 [skill-rendering](skill-rendering.md) process once this definition 128 stands approved. Until that run the carrier does not exist, so its 129 correspondence to this definition cannot be walked at screening time: 130 skill-rendering's own check — a fresh render diffed against what 131 stands — is the check of that correspondence, as it is for every 132 approved process. 133 134 ## Flow (compiled) 135 136 Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not 137 edit by hand. 138 139 ```mermaid 140 flowchart TD 141 enumerate["Enumerate the qualifying typedefs — runtime
in — definitions: string
out — approved: string[]"] 142 check["Check the load points against a fresh render — runtime
in — approved: string[], compiler: string, guidelines: string, fitness: string
out — findings: string[]"] 143 filter["Filter the findings to the rows still open — runtime
in — findings: string[], escalations: string[]
out — open: string[]"] 144 route{"Route on the open rows
in — open: string[], escalations: string[], round: integer, round_cap: integer"} 145 reconcile(["Reconcile the open rows — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], guidelines: string, fitness: string, compiler: string, escalations: string[]
out — escalations: string[]"]) 146 advance_round["Advance the round — runtime
in — round: integer
sets — round: integer"] 147 report(["Report the rows left open — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], escalations: string[], self: string
out — escalations: string[]"]) 148 __end(("end")) 149 __start(("start")) --> enumerate 150 enumerate --> check 151 check --> filter 152 filter --> route 153 route -->|success exit: check clean, nothing escalated — every qualifying typedef's two texts current| __end 154 route -->|success exit: no row open — escalations filed through report| report 155 route -->|failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with rows open| report 156 route -->|else| reconcile 157 reconcile --> advance_round 158 advance_round --> check 159 report --> __end 160 ``` 161 162 163 ## Data 164 165 Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema 166 names inline; conditions are CEL expressions over these names. Paths 167 are relative to the lead shop's repository root, the run's working 168 directory. The definition of good for this process is the feature 169 [feat-typedef-rendering](../../features/feat-typedef-rendering.md); 170 each outcome names the scenarios it witnesses. The design decision the 171 process rests on is 172 [adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering](../../decisions/adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering.md). 173 `definitions` names the directory of the lead shop's typedefs and 174 nothing else. A typedef *qualifies* when its front-matter carries 175 `status: approved` and its body carries the second-level headings 176 `## Writing rules` and `## Fitness scenarios` — the sections the 177 artifact-typedef typedef requires of a type whose texts are produced 178 (its required sections 6 and 7) and the compiler reads; `enumerate` 179 tests exactly that, and `approved` is the one 180 enumeration of what qualifies — `check` runs the compiler over that 181 list and no other, so no second reading of "qualifying" can disagree 182 with `enumerate`. `guidelines` and `fitness` are the two load points; a type's texts 183 stand there as `/.md` and 184 `/.fitness.md`, `` the typedef's `defines` value, 185 the compiler's own naming — a qualifying typedef with no `defines` key 186 is a `will-not-compile` row, so the sweep skips it; they are the 187 compiler's own output homes, and this process names them so the sweep and the 188 re-render act on the same paths. `compiler` is the tool: run as 189 `python3 --guideline --fitness ` it 190 produces the type's two texts together, each with front-matter that 191 carries `generated`, `source` — the typedef's path as `approved` lists 192 it — and `source-digest`; run with `--check` it renders to scratch and 193 diffs against what stands, printing its rows or nothing, and never 194 writes a load point — the load points are written only at 195 reconciliation's re-render, where that write is the point. `self` is 196 this definition, the governed record a path-only escalation lands in. 197 A write to a typedef whose path is listed in `approved` — the review 198 entry `reconcile` or `report` puts in its Document History — is a 199 write to a declared input, as role-rendering's steps of the same names 200 make; no output is declared for it. `findings` holds every row the 201 check writes, one per line, in the five kinds O4 names. A `string[]` 202 value interpolates newline-joined into a `run` script — one row per 203 line, so rows may carry spaces and word-splitting is never the 204 contract for a row list; `filter.run` and `check.run` quote each 205 interpolation of a row list for that reason, while `for def in 206 ${approved}` stands unquoted because there the split into paths is 207 the intent and the paths carry no spaces. `open` holds the rows still 208 to act on — a row is open until its subject, the row's second word, is 209 the first word of a row of `escalations`, matched whole, so a row 210 already filed to the owner recurs in `findings` every round without 211 recurring in `open`. Every row of `escalations` therefore begins with 212 the subject it settles — a typedef's id or path, or a path at a load 213 point — followed by what was filed. A `run` step that exits nonzero is 214 a failed step, not an empty result: the run halts at that step and the 215 failure is reported to the reconciler role — it is never read as empty 216 `findings` and never routed as a clean check. The compiler's rows, not 217 its exit status, are its verdict: its check exits zero with its 218 `missing` and `diverged` rows or with none, exits one with a 219 `will-not-compile` row, and exits two with no row on a usage error, 220 so `check.run` treats a nonzero exit with no row printed as the failed 221 step — the compiler could not check — and a nonzero exit with rows 222 printed as the rows. Two kinds the sibling rendering processes — 223 [skill-rendering](skill-rendering.md) and 224 [role-rendering](role-rendering.md) — report do not apply here and 225 are not written: `unrecognized` — a file at a load point that 226 names no `source` and stands at no qualifying typedef's output path is 227 outside this process, not a finding: the base writing style, the six 228 experience guidelines, and the interaction fitness set have no 229 artifact type behind them, and their source is a question the design 230 decision lists as not decided; and `second-home` — each text has one 231 load point, so no second rendering home exists. During the 232 transition, a hand-written file at a qualifying typedef's output path 233 yields both a `hand-written` row from the sweep and, since it is not 234 byte-equal to a fresh render, a `diverged` row from the compiler; one 235 re-render clears both. The run declares no `result`: `produces` is 236 empty because the run's value is state change — every qualifying 237 typedef's two texts current at their load points — and O1's witness 238 pins it. 239 240 ```yaml 241 data: 242 definitions: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/artifacts} 243 compiler: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/tools/compile_typedef.py} 244 guidelines: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/guidelines} 245 fitness: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/fitness} 246 self: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/processes/typedef-rendering.md} 247 approved: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 248 findings: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 249 open: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 250 escalations: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} 251 round: {type: integer, initial: 1} 252 round_cap: {type: integer, initial: 3} 253 ``` 254 255 ## Steps 256 257 ```yaml 258 start: enumerate 259 steps: 260 - id: enumerate 261 name: Enumerate the qualifying typedefs 262 run-by: {execution: runtime} 263 inputs: [definitions] 264 outputs: [approved] 265 run: | 266 for def in ${definitions}/*.md; do 267 awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit 1} NR > 1 && !body && /^---$/ {body = 1; next} !body && /^status: approved$/ {a = 1} body && /^## Writing rules$/ {w = 1} body && /^## Fitness scenarios$/ {s = 1} END {exit !(a && w && s)}' "$def" \ 268 && printf '%s\n' "$def" 269 done | sort 270 next: check 271 272 - id: check 273 name: Check the load points against a fresh render 274 run-by: {execution: runtime} 275 inputs: [approved, compiler, guidelines, fitness] 276 outputs: [findings] 277 run: | 278 for def in ${approved}; do 279 rows=$(python3 ${compiler} "$def" --check) || { rc=$?; [ -n "$rows" ] || exit $rc; } 280 [ -z "$rows" ] || printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -v def="$def" '$2 != def { $2 = $2 " " def } { print }' 281 done 282 for file in ${guidelines}/*.md ${fitness}/*.md; do 283 [ -f "$file" ] || continue 284 src=$(awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && sub(/^source: */, "") {print; exit}' "$file") 285 [ -z "$src" ] && continue 286 printf '%s\n' "${approved}" | grep -qxF -- "$src" \ 287 || printf 'stale %s %s\n' "$src" "$file" 288 done 289 for def in ${approved}; do 290 type=$(awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && sub(/^defines: */, "") {print; exit}' "$def") 291 [ -n "$type" ] || continue 292 for file in ${guidelines}/$type.md ${fitness}/$type.fitness.md; do 293 [ -f "$file" ] || continue 294 awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^generated:/ {g = 1; exit} END {exit !g}' "$file" \ 295 || printf 'hand-written %s %s\n' "$file" "$def" 296 done 297 done 298 next: filter 299 300 - id: filter 301 name: Filter the findings to the rows still open 302 run-by: {execution: runtime} 303 inputs: [findings, escalations] 304 outputs: [open] 305 run: | 306 printf '%s\n' "${findings}" | while IFS= read -r row; do 307 [ -n "$row" ] || continue 308 subject=$(printf '%s\n' "$row" | cut -d' ' -f2) 309 printf '%s\n' "${escalations}" | cut -d' ' -f1 | grep -qxF -- "$subject" \ 310 || printf '%s\n' "$row" 311 done 312 next: route 313 314 - id: route 315 name: Route on the open rows 316 run-by: {execution: runtime} 317 inputs: [open, escalations, round, round_cap] 318 branches: 319 - label: "success exit: check clean, nothing escalated — every qualifying typedef's two texts current" 320 when: size(open) == 0 && size(escalations) == 0 321 next: end 322 - label: "success exit: no row open — escalations filed through report" 323 when: size(open) == 0 324 next: report 325 - label: "failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with rows open" 326 when: round >= round_cap 327 next: report 328 - else: reconcile 329 330 - id: reconcile 331 name: Reconcile the open rows 332 run-by: {role: lead-solutions-architect, execution: agent} 333 inputs: [open, approved, guidelines, fitness, compiler, escalations] 334 outputs: [escalations] 335 prompt: | 336 Act on each row of open by its kind, the first word; the second 337 word is its subject. Every row you add to escalations begins with 338 that subject as its first word, then what you filed. "missing", 339 "diverged", or "hand-written": re-render — run `python3 340 ${compiler} --guideline ${guidelines}/.md 341 --fitness ${fitness}/.fitness.md`, the row's third 342 word (the typedef's path, listed in approved) and the 343 value of `defines` in that typedef's front-matter; one run produces the type's two texts together 344 and overwrites whatever stands at either path, a hand edit 345 included — reconciliation is the re-render by the compiler, never 346 an edit to a rendered text, and never an edit to the typedef made 347 to match one. "stale": remove the file at the row's third word 348 from its load point; nothing produced from a typedef that does 349 not qualify stays where a maker or a check reads it. 350 "will-not-compile": do not retry; write a review entry into the 351 Document History of the typedef at the subject — its path, 352 listed in approved — naming this process and the row, and add a 353 row to escalations — the subject, then the entry. --- type: process-definition id: typedef-rendering-process owner: product-authority status: draft version: 1 created: 2026-09-05 updated: 2026-09-05 produces: [] carried-by: typedef-rendering-skill condition-language: cel annotations: claude-code: activation: model-judged promotion: experiment-local use-when: "an approved typedef carrying its writing rules and fitness scenarios changes or lands, a guideline or fitness set at its load point stands in doubt — missing, not current with its typedef, written by hand, or left by a typedef that no longer qualifies — or the shop must confirm that every such typedef has both of its texts current" --- # Process: Typedef rendering **Purpose:** Keep the two texts of every artifact type current with the type's one standard. An *artifact type* is a kind of document the shop produces; its *typedef* is the single source the type is generated from, a definition under `basis/artifacts/`. A typedef that stands approved and carries a "Writing rules" section and a "Fitness scenarios" section is the type's standard, and this process calls such a typedef *qualifying*. Its two texts are *renderings* — generated outputs, never edited by hand, never the source: the *guideline*, the maker's text, the type's writing rules read by whoever makes an artifact of the type; and the *fitness set*, the checker's text, the judged Given/When/Then scenarios a check screens an artifact against. Each stands at a *load point*, the directory its readers read it from: `basis/guidelines/` for guidelines and `basis/fitness/` for fitness sets. The process checks what stands at the two load points against a fresh render of each qualifying typedef by the *compiler* — the tool of the *lead shop*, this repository, the shop that owns the product's definitions — that produces both texts from a typedef, and reconciles every difference through the compiler — so that a maker and a checker of the type work from the same words, a change to the typedef reaches both texts, and a clean check is the shop's evidence that they do. **Guiding statement:** A rendering is never the source of truth. Whatever stands at a load point that a fresh render of a qualifying typedef would not put there is a finding, and every finding resolves toward the typedef — a re-render by the compiler, a removal, or the owner's decision on the typedef — never an edit to a rendered text, and never an edit to the typedef made to match one. **Outcomes:** - O1. Every qualifying typedef has both of its texts at their load points, each byte-equal to a fresh render of that typedef, and the check reports no finding of any kind — witnessed by `route`'s first success exit, on empty `open` with empty `escalations` (feature scenarios 3 and 5: after a run, each text is current with its typedef as it now stands). - O2. The texts land where the checks already read, and nowhere else: a type's guideline at `/.md` and its fitness set at `/.fitness.md`, `` the type key the typedef's `defines` names — the paths the artifact checks and the linter read today — so a check finds the checker's text where it read it before and no check's definition changes for this — witnessed by `reconcile`'s render into those two paths and by `check`'s sweep of those two directories and no other (feature scenario 6). The scenario's other half — a check running from its definition as it stood, its Document History recording no change — is witnessed at delivery, in that check's Document History, not by a step of this process. - O3. A typedef that does not qualify yields no text a maker or a check reads: `enumerate` admits only qualifying typedefs and its list is the set `check` renders against, and a `stale` rendering (O4) is removed at reconciliation — witnessed by `enumerate`'s run, its `approved` read by `check`, and the stale rows of `open` consumed by `reconcile` (the feature's constraint C6). - O4. The check reports every defect as a row of one of five kinds, named here and nowhere else. The row's first word is the kind and its second word its subject; for `missing`, `diverged`, `hand-written`, and `stale` the third word is the path the reconciliation acts on, and `will-not-compile` acts on its subject and carries the reason as the remainder. Three kinds are the compiler's rows, one run per typedef in `approved`: `missing ` — a text absent from its load point; `diverged ` — a text not byte-equal to a fresh render of its typedef, whatever the cause, a hand edit or a typedef amended after its render — where `` is the produced text's id, `-guideline` or `-fitness`, so the row names the text, and `` is the typedef's path, added by `check` as the third word, so the row names the type; `will-not-compile ` — a typedef in `approved` the compiler does not render, its subject the typedef's path as the compiler prints it, and for which the compiler writes no `missing` or `diverged` row, so an unrenderable typedef never also burns the run toward the cap. Two kinds are `check`'s own sweep of the load points: `stale ` — a rendering whose `source` key names a typedef not in `approved`; `hand-written ` — a file at a qualifying typedef's output path that carries no `generated` key; the subject of a sweep row is a path — witnessed by the rows of `findings` that `check` writes (feature scenario 4). - O5. Every finding reaches its consumer and resolves toward the typedef: `missing`, `diverged`, and `hand-written` are re-rendered by the compiler, which produces the type's two texts together, so both are current with the typedef as it now stands after reconciliation; `stale` is removed; `will-not-compile` lands as a review entry in that typedef's Document History. An escalation never ends with the run and never burns it: a row whose subject is already named in `escalations` is not open, so a check clean of open rows with escalations standing routes through `report`, which files each row into the governed record the owner reads — witnessed by `filter`'s run, `reconcile`'s prompt, `route`'s clean-with-escalations branch, and `report`'s prompt (feature scenarios 3 and 5). **Roles:** reconciler and reporter — [`../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md`](../roles/lead-solutions-architect.md) (the compilers and the lint are this role's apparatus; it consumes the check's findings, and its resulting action per finding is a re-render, a removal, or an escalation). The owner — the product authority, who owns and approves every typedef — decides every escalated typedef change; that decision lands through governed evolution, not through a step of this process. The check itself is mechanical and runs by the runtime against the qualifying typedefs and the compiler's rendering contract, so the definition of good sits outside the role that reconciles. **Carried by:** `.claude/skills/typedef-rendering/SKILL.md` — generated from this definition by [`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never edited by hand, and placed at the skills load point by the [skill-rendering](skill-rendering.md) process once this definition stands approved. Until that run the carrier does not exist, so its correspondence to this definition cannot be walked at screening time: skill-rendering's own check — a fresh render diffed against what stands — is the check of that correspondence, as it is for every approved process. ## Flow (compiled) Generated from the steps below by `tools/compile_process.py`; do not edit by hand. ```mermaid flowchart TD enumerate["Enumerate the qualifying typedefs — runtime
in — definitions: string
out — approved: string[]"] check["Check the load points against a fresh render — runtime
in — approved: string[], compiler: string, guidelines: string, fitness: string
out — findings: string[]"] filter["Filter the findings to the rows still open — runtime
in — findings: string[], escalations: string[]
out — open: string[]"] route{"Route on the open rows
in — open: string[], escalations: string[], round: integer, round_cap: integer"} reconcile(["Reconcile the open rows — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], guidelines: string, fitness: string, compiler: string, escalations: string[]
out — escalations: string[]"]) advance_round["Advance the round — runtime
in — round: integer
sets — round: integer"] report(["Report the rows left open — agent: lead-solutions-architect
in — open: string[], approved: string[], escalations: string[], self: string
out — escalations: string[]"]) __end(("end")) __start(("start")) --> enumerate enumerate --> check check --> filter filter --> route route -->|success exit: check clean, nothing escalated — every qualifying typedef's two texts current| __end route -->|success exit: no row open — escalations filed through report| report route -->|failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — report with rows open| report route -->|else| reconcile reconcile --> advance_round advance_round --> check report --> __end ``` ## Data Each entry names a process-local value. Simple types use JSON Schema names inline; conditions are CEL expressions over these names. Paths are relative to the lead shop's repository root, the run's working directory. The definition of good for this process is the feature [feat-typedef-rendering](../../features/feat-typedef-rendering.md); each outcome names the scenarios it witnesses. The design decision the process rests on is [adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering](../../decisions/adr-2026-09-05-typedef-rendering.md). `definitions` names the directory of the lead shop's typedefs and nothing else. A typedef *qualifies* when its front-matter carries `status: approved` and its body carries the second-level headings `## Writing rules` and `## Fitness scenarios` — the sections the artifact-typedef typedef requires of a type whose texts are produced (its required sections 6 and 7) and the compiler reads; `enumerate` tests exactly that, and `approved` is the one enumeration of what qualifies — `check` runs the compiler over that list and no other, so no second reading of "qualifying" can disagree with `enumerate`. `guidelines` and `fitness` are the two load points; a type's texts stand there as `/.md` and `/.fitness.md`, `` the typedef's `defines` value, the compiler's own naming — a qualifying typedef with no `defines` key is a `will-not-compile` row, so the sweep skips it; they are the compiler's own output homes, and this process names them so the sweep and the re-render act on the same paths. `compiler` is the tool: run as `python3 --guideline --fitness ` it produces the type's two texts together, each with front-matter that carries `generated`, `source` — the typedef's path as `approved` lists it — and `source-digest`; run with `--check` it renders to scratch and diffs against what stands, printing its rows or nothing, and never writes a load point — the load points are written only at reconciliation's re-render, where that write is the point. `self` is this definition, the governed record a path-only escalation lands in. A write to a typedef whose path is listed in `approved` — the review entry `reconcile` or `report` puts in its Document History — is a write to a declared input, as role-rendering's steps of the same names make; no output is declared for it. `findings` holds every row the check writes, one per line, in the five kinds O4 names. A `string[]` value interpolates newline-joined into a `run` script — one row per line, so rows may carry spaces and word-splitting is never the contract for a row list; `filter.run` and `check.run` quote each interpolation of a row list for that reason, while `for def in ${approved}` stands unquoted because there the split into paths is the intent and the paths carry no spaces. `open` holds the rows still to act on — a row is open until its subject, the row's second word, is the first word of a row of `escalations`, matched whole, so a row already filed to the owner recurs in `findings` every round without recurring in `open`. Every row of `escalations` therefore begins with the subject it settles — a typedef's id or path, or a path at a load point — followed by what was filed. A `run` step that exits nonzero is a failed step, not an empty result: the run halts at that step and the failure is reported to the reconciler role — it is never read as empty `findings` and never routed as a clean check. The compiler's rows, not its exit status, are its verdict: its check exits zero with its `missing` and `diverged` rows or with none, exits one with a `will-not-compile` row, and exits two with no row on a usage error, so `check.run` treats a nonzero exit with no row printed as the failed step — the compiler could not check — and a nonzero exit with rows printed as the rows. During the transition, a hand-written file at a qualifying typedef's output path yields both a `hand-written` row from the sweep and, since it is not byte-equal to a fresh render, a `diverged` row from the compiler; one re-render clears both. The run declares no `result`: `produces` is empty because the run's value is state change — every qualifying typedef's two texts current at their load points — and O1's witness pins it. ```yaml data: definitions: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/artifacts} compiler: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/tools/compile_typedef.py} guidelines: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/guidelines} fitness: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/fitness} self: {type: string, format: uri-reference, initial: basis/processes/typedef-rendering.md} approved: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} findings: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} open: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} escalations: {type: array, items: {type: string}, initial: []} round: {type: integer, initial: 1} round_cap: {type: integer, initial: 3} ``` ## Steps ```yaml start: enumerate steps: - id: enumerate name: Enumerate the qualifying typedefs run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [definitions] outputs: [approved] run: | for def in ${definitions}/*.md; do awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit 1} NR > 1 && !body && /^---$/ {body = 1; next} !body && /^status: approved$/ {a = 1} body && /^## Writing rules$/ {w = 1} body && /^## Fitness scenarios$/ {s = 1} END {exit !(a && w && s)}' "$def" \ && printf '%s\n' "$def" done | sort next: check - id: check name: Check the load points against a fresh render run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [approved, compiler, guidelines, fitness] outputs: [findings] run: | for def in ${approved}; do rows=$(python3 ${compiler} "$def" --check) || { rc=$?; [ -n "$rows" ] || exit $rc; } [ -z "$rows" ] || printf '%s\n' "$rows" | awk -v def="$def" '$2 != def { $2 = $2 " " def } { print }' done for file in ${guidelines}/*.md ${fitness}/*.md; do type=$(awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && sub(/^defines: */, "") {print; exit}' "$def") [ -n "$type" ] || continue for file in ${guidelines}/$type.md ${fitness}/$type.fitness.md; do [ -f "$file" ] || continue awk 'NR == 1 && !/^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^---$/ {exit} NR > 1 && /^generated:/ {g = 1; exit} END {exit !g}' "$file" \ || printf 'hand-written %s %s\n' "$file" "$def" done done next: filter - id: filter name: Filter the findings to the rows still open run-by: {execution: runtime} inputs: [findings, escalations] outputs: [open] run: | printf '%s\n' "${findings}" | while IFS= read -r row; Every row you add to escalations begins with that subject as its first word, then what you filed.
